In [[cryptography]], '''E2''' is a [[Symmetric-key algorithm|symmetric]] [[block cipher]] which was created in 1998 by [[Nippon Telegraph and Telephone|NTT]] and submitted to the [[AES competition]].

Like other AES candidates, E2 operates on blocks of 128 bits, using a key of 128, 192, or 256 bits. It uses a 12-round [[Feistel cipher|Feistel network]]. E2 has an input transformation and output transformation that both use [[modular arithmetic|modular multiplication]], but the round function itself consists only of [[XOR]]s and [[substitution box|S-box]] lookups. The single 8×8-bit S-box is constructed from the composition of an [[affine transformation]] with the discrete [[exponentiation]] x<sup>127</sup> over the [[finite field]] GF(2<sup>8</sup>). NTT adopted many of E2's special characteristics in [[Camellia (cipher)|Camellia]], which has essentially replaced E2.
